meta.storyTitle: Design the fix for ISSUE-c5b49ff953a9a295: every trivial change gets an ISSUE record (triage routes trivial to the issue stage, approval advances to build), the ISSUE can describe a non-defect change, steering/guide text updated, approving a trivial BUILD completes its Story, and a deliberate decision for the 16 existing headless trivial builds.

q7aeab4c0.question: q1: The 16 existing headless trivial builds. Recommended: leave them and record the decision, because a backfilled ISSUE would be system-written after the fact, not a person-reviewed trace. Alternative: a one-off repair that writes a kind 'change' ISSUE from each BUILD's focus under its own hash, approved by the migration actor, then completes each Story.
q7aeab4c0.choice: Backfill: a one-off repair writes an ISSUE (kind 'change') for each of the 16 existing headless trivial builds from its BUILD's request text (focus and triage rationale), under the BUILD's own hash, approved by the migration actor with the reason recorded, then completes each Story through the existing completion walk.
q7aeab4c0.rationale: User decision 2026-11-15: chose the backfill alternative over leaving the 16 builds headless.

summary.prose: A trivial change now starts with an ISSUE record, like a small bugfix. Triage routes trivial work to the issue stage; the ISSUE says it is a change rather than a defect and is worded that way. Approving it hands build the ISSUE's own hash, so the build, its review and its Story completion all hang off that record. Build no longer invents a new work item for a no-design build, so neither a trivial change nor a small bugfix can end up without its ISSUE.

hldContextSlice.frameworkSummary: Standalone feature — no parent HLD. Design directly against the repo, grounded on the s1 analyze passes. There are no HLD shared contracts to honour.

dataModelChanges.details: Optional kind: 'defect' | 'change'. Absent means 'defect', so every stored ISSUE keeps its meaning and rendering. Set from the issue run's params.kind ('change' for a trivial triage result). The body fields (title, reproduction, rootCause, fixIntent) keep their names and validator; for a change they hold what was asked, why, and the change. magnitude stays 'small' | 'sized'; a trivial change carries 'small'.
A no-LLD standalone build must carry epicHash naming an approved ISSUE. The focus-derived hash is no longer minted.

errorCases.scenario: An agent calls insrc_build_step for a no-LLD standalone build without epicHash (an old steering copy, a hand-written call, or a caller that dropped it).
errorCases.detection: handleStandaloneImplement finds ctx.epicHash undefined for a sizeClass 'trivial' call, where it used to call standaloneEpicHashFromFocus.
errorCases.response: Return BuildStepError 'no-identity' naming the fix: run insrc_triage, approve the ISSUE, then build with its hash. Nothing is written.
errorCases.userImpact: The build does not start until an ISSUE exists; no headless record is created.

errorCases.scenario: A no-LLD standalone build names an epicHash with no ISSUE, or with an ISSUE that is still pending.
errorCases.detection: Admission reads the ISSUE head for the hash and finds it missing or its lifecycle not approved.
errorCases.response: Refuse with 'no-head' (missing) or the existing unapproved-upstream refusal (pending), naming the ISSUE id.
errorCases.userImpact: The user approves the ISSUE first; the build then proceeds under it.

errorCases.scenario: An approved ISSUE reaches the advance without a usable issueHash.
errorCases.response: Throw; the approval's followOn reports bugfix-advance ok:false with the message, as for an invalid magnitude today.
errorCases.userImpact: The ISSUE stays approved; the agent sees the failed advance instead of a call that would build headless.

errorCases.scenario: An ISSUE written with kind 'change' is read by a client built before this change.
errorCases.response: It renders the defect headings over the change text; the record and routing stay correct.
errorCases.userImpact: Wording only, until the client updates.

migration.stateBefore: Triage routes trivial work straight to build (routeForSizeClass returns startStage 'build'; the triage nextCall is insrc_build_step '(standalone-trivial)' with no epicHash). Build mints a work-item hash from the focus text for a no-LLD call (standaloneEpicHashFromFocus). The small-bugfix advance also emits its build call without the ISSUE's hash. A headless trivial build cannot complete its Story because requireEpicAnchor reads only the head. The steering block tells agents a standalone BUILD record is a trivial change's ledger entry. 16 approved headless trivial BUILD records exist in this repository, none with a STORY record.
migration.stateAfter: Triage routes trivial work to the issue stage (sizeClass trivial, magnitude small, kind change). The ISSUE renders change wording when meta.kind is 'change'. Approving any small or sized ISSUE hands the next stage the ISSUE's hash. Build refuses a no-LLD call without an epicHash naming an approved ISSUE, so no new headless build can be made. Approving a trivial BUILD completes its Story under the ISSUE. The steering text says trivial work starts with an ISSUE. The 16 existing headless builds are handled as decided in the open question below.

migrationSteps.action: Add optional meta.kind ('defect' | 'change') to IssueArtifact; absent reads as 'defect'. Teach the renderer and the issue.capture prompt the change wording. Stored ISSUEs are untouched and render byte-identically.
Make nextAfterIssue put the ISSUE's hash into the emitted build call (standalone.epicHash) and design.story call (params.epicHash), refusing an ISSUE without a 16-hex issueHash.
Flip routeForSizeClass('trivial') to startStage 'issue' and change the triage nextCall to start the issue workflow with sizeClass trivial, magnitude small, kind change. Update the route tests.
Make the standalone no-LLD build refuse a call without epicHash (no-identity) or whose epicHash has no approved ISSUE (no-head), replacing the focus-derived hash.

Update the steering block (triage route list, build guide, code-review pinning rule, triage skip rule) so trivial work starts with an ISSUE and pins it in the code-review packet; refresh assets/steering-block.md through the plugin's sync-assets.

Existing headless trivial builds: apply the decision recorded for open question q1. Recommended: leave the 16 records as they are and record the decision in BUILD.md, because a backfilled ISSUE would be written by the system after the fact rather than reviewed by a person, which is the trace the rule asks for. The alternative is a one-off repair that writes an ISSUE (kind change) from each BUILD's focus and triage rationale under the BUILD's own hash, approved by the migration actor with the reason recorded, after which the existing completion walk completes each Story.

migration.backwardCompat: IssueArtifact gains an optional field; old ISSUEs read and render as before, and an old client renders a change ISSUE with defect headings (wording only). The triage nextCall for trivial changes shape (issue workflow instead of build); agents follow nextCall verbatim, and the steering text changes in the same release. insrc_build_step now refuses a no-LLD standalone call without epicHash: a caller relying on the minted hash (an old steering copy or a hand-written call) gets a no-identity error that names the issue stage, instead of a headless build. Small (LLD) standalone builds are unchanged.

alternativesConsidered.name: Issue stage first, with a change kind
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Triage routes trivial to the issue stage; the ISSUE records a change kind; approval advances to build carrying the ISSUE's hash; build refuses a headless trivial build.
alternativesConsidered.approach: routeForSizeClass('trivial') returns startStage 'issue' with producesLld false, and triage's nextCall starts the issue workflow (as for a small bugfix) with sizeClass 'trivial'. The IssueArtifact meta gains kind: 'defect' | 'change' (absent reads as defect, so every existing ISSUE is unchanged). For a change, the capture prompt asks what was asked and why, and the document renders 'What was asked' / 'Why' / 'Change' in place of Reproduction / Root cause / Fix intent; the body fields keep their names. The issue-approval advance (nextAfterIssue) routes a trivial ISSUE, and a small bugfix, to build and puts the ISSUE's hash in standalone.epicHash. The standalone no-LLD build stops minting a hash from the focus and refuses a call with no epicHash, so no new headless build can be made. Steering and guide text change to match. The 16 headless builds are handled by a repair step (see migration).
pros: Every trivial change and every small bugfix gets a reviewed ISSUE record, the user's rule.
Story completion works with no change to the anchor rules: the ISSUE is the head.
Closes the second route: a small bugfix followed verbatim no longer builds headless.
Reuses the existing issue stage, advance seam and route table; no new record kind.
cons: Adds one approval stop (the ISSUE) before every trivial build.
Touches triage, the issue artifact and prompt, the advance, build-step identity and steering text.

alternativesConsidered.name: Issue stage first, neutral wording, no kind
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Same routing as a1, but the ISSUE is reworded to fit both defects and changes instead of carrying a kind.
alternativesConsidered.approach: Routing, the advance carrying the ISSUE's hash and the build refusing a headless trivial call are as in a1. Instead of a kind field, the capture prompt and the rendered headings become neutral for every ISSUE ('Problem or request', 'Cause or motivation', 'Intended change'). No meta field is added.
pros: No new meta field or validator change.
cons: Rewords every existing and future defect ISSUE, which loses the sharp reproduction / root-cause framing defects need.
Downstream readers (the GitHub issue body, reviewers) cannot tell a defect from a change.
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Same routing as a1 but fi2 is only partial: rewording every ISSUE degrades defect records to avoid one optional meta field.

alternativesConsidered.name: Build writes the ISSUE itself
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Keep trivial routed to build, but build's implement phase writes an ISSUE head from the focus before it starts.
alternativesConsidered.approach: Triage keeps startStage 'build'. When a standalone trivial build has no head, implement writes an IssueArtifact (kind change) from the focus and triage rationale under the build's hash, approved by the system rather than a person, then builds. Completion then finds the ISSUE head.
pros: No extra approval stop for trivial work.
Every trivial build gets a head and its Story completes.
cons: The ISSUE is never reviewed or approved by a person, so it records the agent's own wording only.
A system-approved head bypasses the human approval gate the workflow relies on for every other head.
Build writes a design-stage record, mixing stage responsibilities.
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Avoids the extra stop but violates the human-approval rule for heads and only partly meets fi1.

alternativesConsidered.name: Anchor fallback only
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Leave routing as it is; let Story completion take the anchor from the BUILD record's stamp.
alternativesConsidered.approach: requireEpicAnchor (or the creation context) falls back to the work item's BUILD record epicCreatedAt when there is no head, as record path resolution already does. Trivial work stays headless; approving its BUILD now completes its Story.
pros: Smallest change; existing headless builds could complete without new records.
cons: Does not meet the user's rule: no ISSUE record, so the trace is still lost.
Leaves the small-bugfix advance building headless.
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Fixes only fi4; the trace stays lost, which is the user's actual requirement.

openQuestions: q1: The 16 existing headless trivial builds. Recommended: leave them and record the decision, because a backfilled ISSUE would be system-written after the fact, not a person-reviewed trace. Alternative: a one-off repair that writes a kind 'change' ISSUE from each BUILD's focus under its own hash, approved by the migration actor, then completes each Story.
ts1: The Story carries no acceptance criteria of its own; ac1-ac5 are the five fix-intent points of ISSUE-c5b49ff953a9a295.

sequenceDefinition.narrative: The trivial path after the fix: triage starts the issue stage, the user approves the ISSUE, the advance hands build the ISSUE's hash, and approving the BUILD completes the Story under that ISSUE.
